title: Nimble commit bands and ops velocity playbook for Private/VPC packaging
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Goal: Design and validate a flexible licensing and support playbook that reduces sales friction for Private/VPC and on-prem customers while preserving predictable revenue and enabling fast emergency patching. The playbook centers on two linked experiments: (1) Nimble commit bands — narrow commitment ranges with built-in short-term burst credits and automatic rebalancing; (2) Ops Velocity tiers — a support/upgrade cadence tied to an "ops velocity" SLA metric that captures upgrade turnaround, emergency patching time, and escalation path responsiveness. Deliver a recommended pricing matrix, contract language snippets for RFIs/SQs, and a pilot for 3 mid-market accounts.
acceptance_criteria: Experiment matrix defined with 3 commit band sizes and pricing differential
Ops Velocity tier definitions (Standard, Fast, Critical) with measurable SLOs and corresponding support fees
Contract clauses drafted for upgrade cadence windows and emergency patch credits
Security questionnaire (SQ) answers prepared for top 20 enterprise questions and flagged open items for Legal/Security
Pilot sign-ups from at least 2 existing private-deploy prospects and baseline telemetry to measure cost/revenue impact
updates: 2025-03-01: Ticket created; scoped two coordinated experiments and pilot plan. Initial stakeholder list: Sales (J. Morales), Legal (S. Patel), Security (R. Ahmed), Engineering (L. Chen), Solutions Eng (T. Ruiz).

2025-03-04: Workshop with Sales and Solutions to map common procurement blockers (maintenance windows, upgrade frequency, patch SLA). Sales feedback: buyers want narrow commit bands to avoid long-term lock-in but need price predictability.

2025-03-06: Drafted three commit band profiles: Entry (3-6 month, 0-5% burst credits), Mid (6-12 month, 10% burst), Anchor (12+ month, 25% burst + discounted rate). Shared pricing delta estimates with Finance.

2025-03-08: Security queued the SQ response set; identified 6 high-risk items (KMS/HSM key escrow, data residency attestations, upgrade rollback guarantees). Asked Legal for playbook contract language to handle escrow and rollback liability.

2025-03-10: Engineering feasibility check: autoscale burst credits require changes to Dedicated token accounting and billing hooks (ENG-84210). Estimated 2 sprints of infra work for safe metering and automatic rebalancing. Added dependency.

2025-03-11: Created pilot outreach list and initial email template. Target pilot accounts: Acme Analytics (mid-market), HelixHealth (regulated), Nimbus Retail (SaaS). Sales committed to run 2 pilots this quarter.

2025-03-12: PM/Design review scheduled for 2025-03-14 to finalize pricing tiers and contract snippets. Next steps: finalize SQ answers draft, confirm engineering estimate for meter changes, and prepare pilot contract addendum template.
risks: Engineering effort to implement burst credit metering may slip, delaying pilot launch
Legal negotiation around rollback and escrow language could add 2-4 weeks
Customers may prefer fixed-fee plus overage rather than commit bands, affecting pilot conversion
mitigations: Scope pilot to use manual billing adjustments if automated metering not ready
Prepare fallback contract language that offers time-limited escrow acceptance while Legal completes review
Run A/B with one pilot on fixed-fee plus overage to measure preference vs commit-bands
notes_for_sales_playbook: Use 'Nimble Commit' framing to emphasize flexibility: short bands + burst credits provide hedge against growth uncertainty
Highlight Ops Velocity as an operational SLA purchasers can buy up to reduce upgrade wait times
Provide templated addendum for pilots that captures pilot duration, metrics to measure, and exit terms
